correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary center, reflecting both base slices gives two necessary and sufficient support-function inequalities. Symmetry of the bases makes the spatial-zero center feasible exactly when a 2-variable linear program in U,V is feasible; no competing nonzero spatial translation can evade those necessary inequalities. Solving the planar LP by its two coordinate corners and simultaneous active intersection yields the formula with uniqueness of the height. Substitution gives the complete fiber. Box support functions reduce all directions to axis conditions and prove its exact product structure. The strict bound 3 and a crossed-box sharpness sequence are algebraic. The packaged standard-library exact-rational checker independently enumerates LP vertices in 1320 cases and checks 46200 sampled support inequalities. Finite checks alone do not establish the universal theorem.

value.rationale: The gap is the global Minkowski-center geometry of a natural nonhomothetic two-layer convex hull. The classification replaces infinitely many support constraints in the scalar optimization by two measurable containment ratios, identifies all transitions and full center fibers, and yields an exact dimension formula for a natural independently scaled orthotope family. The strict dimension-independent asymmetry bound below three with sharp crossed-box limit is geometrically nontrivial; homothetic specializations cannot explain its mixed regime.
